chunks: It was narrated by Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Naṣr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام: A man adopts a dwelling, then passes by it; should he perform in full or shorten? He said: Every dwelling that you do not reside in as a homeland is not a dwelling for you, and it is not for you to perform in full therein.

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلٍ: as a recognized dwelling for legal purposes
key_terms.تَسْتَوْطِنُهُ: you take it as a settled homeland or place of residence
key_terms.يَمُرُّ: he passes by it during travel
key_terms.يُتِمُّ: he performs the salat (prayer) in full
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: he shortens the salat (prayer) as a traveler

ai.seo_question: If a traveler passes by a property or dwelling he owns but does not reside in, should he shorten or complete the salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the traveler’s salat (prayer) when passing through a place he has taken as a dwelling. The Imam عليه السلام states that a place is not treated as one’s true residence unless it is actually inhabited as a home, and therefore one does not perform the prayer in full there.
